source.title: Hypothesis: gradient descent prefers general circuits

record.file_problem: none; full post and comments are present.
record.tranche_reason: The post mainly proposes an unconfirmed explanation, but its comments report informal learning-rate experiments on grokking tasks and describe the resulting train/validation behavior. These results bear on grokking and on whether learning-rate choices alter it.
record.gate_note: The main post's circuit diagrams and explanations are hypotheses, not experiments. Results from the cited Grokking paper and the linked replication are cited evidence and are not rows. Rows below cover only experiments described in the post's comments, including brief summaries of linked reports; several are incompletely specified.
record.test_reason: The post's mechanism is an untested hypothesis. Its comments include informal re-implementation runs on algorithmic tasks, reported qualitatively. In the default settings these runs bear weakly on V1, since they say when training accuracy saturates and when validation accuracy rises. The learning-rate interventions measure how LR changes alter convergence. They do not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or softmax precision (V7), or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it should separate the speakers. Pope's account (SGD prefers circuits that predict more training points; regularization and stochasticity remove shallow circuits) is an explicitly unconfirmed hypothesis. In the comments, Lieberum finds LR effects inconsistent across tasks and suggests they reflect a global property of the loss landscape. Pope sees a 'mode shift' to train and validation rising together. Rohin concludes you cannot simply 10x the LR once grokking starts.
record.recipe_differences: The reported experiments are informal learning-rate interventions on grokking tasks, including modular addition, modular division, and permutation group S_5. The post does not provide enough details to establish that the original training recipe was reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported grokking outcomes vary with learning-rate magnitude and when it is changed, and differ across modular-division and S_5 experiments. The counting of grokking time also varies with the chosen onset criterion.

fits_no_version.finding: Raising the learning rate after memorization makes training accuracy fall to validation level, after which both rise together. The 50x run converges; the 10x run diverges again. In modular division, 5x LR helps from the start but destroys progress if switched on later; in S5, LR increases never work.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The train/validation gap characteristic of grokking depends on learning-rate magnitude and timing, which can shift training to a regime where train and validation accuracy rise together.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing LR (5x–10x) once grokking has begun can speed validation convergence. Rohin Shah reads it as 1700 steps down to 150 steps in one setting; 100x breaks training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The speed of the grokking phase scales with the learning rate within a stable range.

record.problems: The proposed circuit mechanism is not experimentally tested. Comment experiments are informal, often reported only qualitatively, and several omit task, model, or hyperparameter details. Some results are available only through linked reports or figures; the text notes a possibly improper dataset split in one run.
record.rows_left_out: No results from the cited Grokking paper or linked replication were included because they are cited work, not experiments conducted in this post. Hypothetical circuit explanations and proposed experiments are not results.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks, and whether validation accuracy starts at chance, are not reported. All results are qualitative.
No test of adaptive-optimizer instabilities or softmax floating-point limits. Only learning-rate magnitude and timing are varied.

missing.what: In the S5 default setting, validation accuracy is ~0.5 when training accuracy reaches 1, consistent with learning only commutativity. True grokking comes later, around 1.5k steps.
missing.locator: Comments, Rohin Shah reply to the S_5 report

missing.what: Rohin Shah's estimate that 10x LR shortens the grokking stage from ~1700 to ~150 steps. He also notes that in Pope's run, 10x LR still leaves the grokking phase at ~8×10^4 steps, the majority of training.
missing.locator: Comments, Rohin Shah replies to Lieberum and Pope

record.verdict_notes: Informal blog post; comment experiments are qualitative, with results mainly in linked wandb reports not in the text. Neither original source is involved. Task identity for Lieberum's first experiment is ambiguous. V7 is not tested: learning-rate scaling is not the optimizer-instability or numerical-precision artifact V7 names.

versions.untested_parts: The reported experiments do not test how grokking delay changes as training-set size shrinks, and do not establish that validation accuracy begins at chance in each run.
No circuits or mechanisms are measured; the gradual unification account is proposed, not experimentally tested.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm/lazy-to-rich comparison is reported.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
Weight decay and low-norm circuit efficiency are discussed, but the experiments do not test the efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs is reported.
The comments vary learning rates but do not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities, softmax floating-point limits, or whether controlling those artifacts eliminates grokking.

relationships.condition: Informal re-implementations (Lieberum) on modular addition and modular division, default settings
relationships.reason: Delays are short or absent: in r12 train 100% at 500 steps, val complete ~2000, curves overlap, split possibly leaky; in r13 grokking is faster than memorization (~1000 vs ~1500 steps).
relationships.display_finding: One run reached 100% training accuracy at 500 steps and complete validation accuracy around 2,000 with overlapping curves and possible split leakage; another generalized around 1,000 steps before memorizing around 1,500.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Grokking is reported after training accuracy reaches 100% in the modular-addition run, and it persists in the stated full-batch/no-regularization setting, though at a reduced level (r12, r14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported timing is not consistently a long delay, and changed learning rates can make training and validation accuracy rise together, fail to work, or disrupt progress (r5-r11, r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Learning-rate effects vary by magnitude, timing, and task: some changes speed progress, while others fail or destroy it; the comments do not establish that optimizer artifacts cause the original delay or that controlling them removes it (r1-r3, r5-r11).
